Title: Description of the experiences of Deng Yingchao, a young Chinese woman during the protests of 1919
Content: When the `text(May Fourth)` Movement took place in `1919`, I was only `text(sixteen years)` old, a student at the Tianjin Women's Normal College... On `text(May 4, 1919)`, students in Beijing held a demonstration asking the government to refuse to sign the Versailles Peace Treaty and to punish the traitors at home. In their indignation [displeasure], they burned the house at Zhaojialou and beat up Lu Zhongxiang, then Chinese envoy to Japan. The following `text(day)`, when the news reached Tianjin, it aroused the indignation of students there who staged their own demonstration on `text(May)` `7^text(th)`. They began by organizing such patriotic societies as the Tianjin Student Union, the Tianjin Women's Patriotic Society, and the Tianjin Association of National Salvation. We had no political theory to guide us at that time, only our strong patriotic enthusiasm. In addition to the Beijing students' requests, we demanded, “Abrogate [reject] the `text(Twenty-One)` Demands!” “Boycott Japanese Goods!” and “Buy Chinese-made goods!” Furthermore, we emphatically refused to become slaves to foreign powers!...
